answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 2 times its size, so a group of 33 keys loses far more than 33 single identities would. The crystal graph is rebuilt each epoch, and therefore the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the dawn audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the sonnet checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 11 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
